page_summary:
This research document provides information about the Eric Foss collection related to the Hour 25 science fiction radio program. The collection was donated to the University of California, Riverside in 2011 and is cataloged as MS 054 within the Eaton Collection of Science Fiction and Fantasy at Tomas Rivera Library.

The document provides detailed contact information: UC Riverside Library, Special Collections and University Archives, Tomas Rivera Library, 4th Floor, P.O. Box 5900, Riverside, CA 92517-5900, phone (951) 827-3233, email specialcollections@ucr.edu. The finding aid notes that the collection is unprocessed, meaning contents have not been fully inventoried at the item level and there is no public listing of specific episodes included in the donation.

Hour 25 was a Los Angeles-based science fiction radio program that aired interviews with major SF authors. The program's archive is potentially significant for Dick studies as it may contain audio recordings of Dick appearances or discussions of his work. The document advises researchers to contact Special Collections directly to inquire about specific holdings, particularly regarding recordings from periods when Dick may have been featured on the program.

## Find out how to contact Eric Foss 

Now I have a complete picture. The Eric Foss collection was donated to UC Riverside in 2011. Let me provide the definitive answer. 

The Eric Foss collection on Hour 25 is no longer in private hands — it was donated in 2011 to the University of California, Riverside, Special Collections & University Archives, where it is [1] [2] cataloged as MS 054 within the Eaton Collection of Science Fiction and Fantasy. 

## How to Access the Collection 

The collection is housed at: 

UC Riverside Library — Special Collections & University Archives 

Tomás Rivera Library, 4th Floor P.O. Box 5900 Riverside, CA 92517-5900 

- Phone: (951) 827-3233 

- Email: specialcollections@ucr.edu 

Website: library.ucr.edu/libraries/special-collections-university-archives 

[3] [1] 

## Important Caveats 

" The finding aid explicitly states: This collection is unprocessed. Please contact Special Collections & University Archives regarding the availability of materials for research use.". [1] This means: 

- The contents have not been fully inventoried at the item level, so there is no public listing of which specific Hour 25 episodes are included in the Foss donation. 

- You would need to contact them directly (email or phone) to ask whether any recordings from September/October 1972 are present in the collection — specifically the Philip K. Dick/Norman Spinrad broadcast. 

## What's in the Collection 

The Foss collection consists of 0.42 linear feet (1 box) of DVDs containing recordings and tapings of various Hour 25 broadcasts, covering the date range 1972–1976. The fact that it spans back to 1972 — the very first year of the show — is promising for your search, since the Dick/Spinrad broadcast occurred on approximately September 29, 1972.[4] [1] 

## Related Collection at UCR 

A separate but related David Bratman collection on Hour 25 was also donated to UC Riverside (in 2013) and contains seven reel-to-reel audio tapes from the show, plus content from L.A.Con I and interviews. This was originally part of the same accession as the Foss donation but was split into its own collection (MS 054a) in 2022 based on provenance. Some of the Bratman tapes have been digitized and are viewable on Calisphere, including panels from L.A.Con I (the 1972 Worldcon that Dick attended).[5] [6] [7] [8] [1] 

## Recommended Next Steps 

- �.Email UC Riverside Special Collections at specialcollections@ucr.edu — explain that you're searching for a specific Hour 25 broadcast from approximately September 29, 1972, featuring Philip K. Dick and Norman Spinrad discussing fascism in science fiction. Ask whether the Foss or Bratman collections contain this recording. 

- �.Contact the Hour 25 Archives — the website hour25.net is maintained by a volunteer archivist (W.W. James) who has been transferring tapes from open reel to CD. The site [9] [10] 

- contact is wwjames@earthlink.net.
